title: validateR
text: Real-world data rarely clean. column might missing values easy overlook. extreme (outlier) values might sneak otherwise normal numeric column. Rows sometimes get duplicated accident data collection merging files. column numeric can end stored text, just entries contain things like "N/" "unknown". column dates can entries don’t match format rest column uses. validateR small set tools helps catch problems affect analysis. checks data frame five common issues: Missing values — many values missing column, percentage represents Outliers — unusually extreme numeric values, detected using IQR method Duplicate rows — rows exact copies , grouped can see rows match Numeric-like inconsistencies — text columns look like meant hold numbers, values don’t convert cleanly Date-like inconsistencies (optional) — text columns look like meant hold dates format specify, values don’t parse cleanly vignette walks complete example: starting messy data frame, running check, reading results.
code: library(validateR)

title: validateR
text: Let’s create small data frame realistic problems: missing value, outlier, duplicated row, text column probably numeric.
code: messy_data <- data.frame(   age = c(25, 12, NA, 17, 19),    weight = c("45", "34", "25", "N/A", "32"),   price = c(100, 120, 140, 1500, 125) ) messy_data <- rbind(messy_data, messy_data[3, ]) messy_data #>    age weight price #> 1   25     45   100 #> 2   12     34   120 #> 3   NA     25   140 #> 4   17    N/A  1500 #> 5   19     32   125 #> 31  NA     25   140

title: validateR

title: Simple Data Frame Validation and Quality Checks
text: validateR lightweight toolkit checking data frames common data quality issues: missing values, outliers, duplicate rows, numeric-like inconsistencies, (optionally) date-like inconsistencies. Results returned structured report object print plot methods, can quickly see ’s wrong data start analyzing .

title: Simple Data Frame Validation and Quality Checks
text: main entry point validate_df(), runs several checks returns single report: can drill full detail behind checks: visualize missing values outliers per column:
code: library(validateR)  messy_df <- data.frame(   age = c(25, 30, NA, 45, 22, 31, 29, 200),   income = c("50000", "62000", "N/A", "48000",              "71000", "55000", "60000", "48000"),   city = c("Thimphu", "Paro", "Thimphu", "Paro",            "Thimphu", "Paro", "Punakha", "Paro"),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) messy_df <- rbind(messy_df, messy_df[1, ], messy_df[4, ])  report <- validate_df(messy_df) report #> < validation_report for 'messy_df' > #> 10 rows, 3 columns #> Checked: 2026-08-11 14:36:44  #>  #> Missing values:          1  column(s) affected #> Outliers:                1  column(s) affected #> Duplicates:              2  group(s) affected #> Numeric-like issues:     1  column(s) affected #> Date-like issues:        NOT checked  #>  #> For details, inspect report$results$missing, $outliers, $duplicates, $numeric_like, $date_like report$results$missing #>   column_name n_missing pct_missing #> 1         age         1          10 #> 2      income         0           0 #> 3        city         0           0 report$results$numeric_like #> $income #> $income$expected_type #> [1] "numeric" #>  #> $income$proportion_convertible #> [1] 90 #>  #> $income$bad_rows #> [1] 3

title: Simple Data Frame Validation and Quality Checks
text: validate_df() can also check whether character columns contain values look like dates format specify. check optional, since date formats ambiguous (example, "03/04/2023" mean March 4th April 3rd, depending convention) — rather guessing, tell format expect column want checked. date_columns isn’t supplied, validate_df() skips date checking entirely, report notes wasn’t checked rather implying column fine:
code: dated_df <- data.frame(   signup_date = c("2023-01-15", "2023-02-20", "not a date",                   "2023-03-10", "2023-04-01"),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  report_with_dates <- validate_df(   dated_df,   date_columns = c(signup_date = "%Y-%m-%d") ) report_with_dates #> < validation_report for 'dated_df' > #> 5 rows, 1 columns #> Checked: 2026-08-11 14:36:44  #>  #> Missing values:          0  column(s) affected #> Outliers:                0  column(s) affected #> Duplicates:              0  group(s) affected #> Numeric-like issues:     0  column(s) affected #> Date-like issues:        1  column(s) affected  #>  #> For details, inspect report$results$missing, $outliers, $duplicates, $numeric_like, $date_like report_without_dates <- validate_df(dated_df) report_without_dates #> < validation_report for 'dated_df' > #> 5 rows, 1 columns #> Checked: 2026-08-11 14:36:44  #>  #> Missing values:          0  column(s) affected #> Outliers:                0  column(s) affected #> Duplicates:              0  group(s) affected #> Numeric-like issues:     0  column(s) affected #> Date-like issues:        NOT checked  #>  #> For details, inspect report$results$missing, $outliers, $duplicates, $numeric_like, $date_like

what: Check for date-like inconsistencies in character columns — check_date_like
title: Check for date-like inconsistencies in character columns — check_date_like
text: Examines specified character columns data frame tests whether non-missing values can parsed dates given format. least 80% (less 100%) column's non-missing values parse successfully, column flagged, row positions non-parsable ("straggler") values reported inspection. Unlike check_numeric_like(), check attempt guess date format automatically - caller must supply expected format column checked, since date formats ambiguous (example, "03/04/2023" mean March 4th April 3rd depending convention) guessing incorrectly silently produce misleading results.

title: Check for date-like inconsistencies in character columns — check_date_like
code: check_date_like(data, date_columns)

title: Check for date-like inconsistencies in character columns — check_date_like
text: data data frame. date_columns named character vector, name column data check, value expected date format column, using format codes accepted base::.Date() (example, "%Y-%m-%d" "%m/%d/%Y"). error raised name date_columns match column data.

title: Check for date-like inconsistencies in character columns — check_date_like
text: named list, one element per flagged column (named column name). element list containing: expected_type Always "date". proportion_parsable_to_date Percentage non-missing values successfully parsed given format, rounded 2 decimals. bad_rows Integer vector row indices whose values parsed given format. Returns empty list columns flagged.

title: Check for date-like inconsistencies in character columns — check_date_like
code: df <- data.frame(   signup_date = c(     "2023-01-15", "2023-02-20", "not a date",     "2023-03-10", "2023-04-01"   ),   notes = c("a", "b", "c", "d", "e") ) check_date_like(df, date_columns = c(signup_date = "%Y-%m-%d")) #> $signup_date #> $signup_date$expected_type #> [1] "date" #>  #> $signup_date$proportion_parsable_to_date #> [1] 80 #>  #> $signup_date$bad_rows #> [1] 3 #>  #>

title: Construct a validation_report object — new_validation_report
text: Low-level constructor assembles already-computed check results single validation_report object. function run checks — simply packages results produced elsewhere (typically check_missing(), check_outliers(), check_duplicates(), check_numeric_like(), check_date_like()) structured, classed object. cases, users call validate_df() instead, runs five checks calls constructor automatically.

text: df data frame checked. Used derive dimensions; stored directly report. df_name character string giving name display data frame printed output. missing_result Output check_missing(). outliers_result Output check_outliers(). duplicates_result Output check_duplicates(). numeric_like_result Output check_numeric_like(). date_like_result Output check_date_like()

title: Construct a validation_report object — new_validation_report
text: object class validation_report, list containing: meta list df_name (character), dim (integer vector rows columns), timestamp (time report created). results list four elements, missing, outliers, duplicates, numeric_like date_like, containing corresponding check results.

title: Construct a validation_report object — new_validation_report
code: df <- data.frame(x = c(1, NA, 3), y = c("a", "b", "c")) report <- new_validation_report(   df = df,   df_name = "df",   missing_result = check_missing(df),   outliers_result = check_outliers(df),   duplicates_result = check_duplicates(df),   numeric_like_result = check_numeric_like(df),   date_like_result = check_date_like(df, date_columns = c(y = "%Y-%m-%d")) ) class(report) #> [1] "validation_report"

what: Validate a data frame for common data quality issues — validate_df
title: Validate a data frame for common data quality issues — validate_df
text: Runs full suite data quality checks data frame — missing values, outliers, duplicate rows, type inconsistencies — returns single, structured report summarizing results. main entry point package; users start rather calling individual check_*() functions directly.

title: Validate a data frame for common data quality issues — validate_df
code: validate_df(data, date_columns = NULL)

title: Validate a data frame for common data quality issues — validate_df
text: data data frame validate. date_columns Optional. named character vector mapping column names data expected date format (using format codes accepted base::.Date()). supplied, check_date_like() run columns fifth check. NULL (default), date checking skipped entirely, report notes checked.

title: Validate a data frame for common data quality issues — validate_df
text: object class validation_report. See new_validation_report() details structure. Printing result shows short summary; full results check available report$results$missing, report$results$outliers, report$results$duplicates, report$results$numeric_like report$results$date_like.

title: Validate a data frame for common data quality issues — validate_df
code: df <- data.frame(   age = c(25, 30, NA, 45, 200),   income = c("50000", "62000", "N/A", "48000", "71000"),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) report <- validate_df(df) report #> < validation_report for 'df' > #> 5 rows, 2 columns #> Checked: 2026-09-12 04:07:46  #>  #> Missing values:          1  column(s) affected #> Outliers:                1  column(s) affected #> Duplicates:              0  group(s) affected #> Numeric-like issues:     1  column(s) affected #> Date-like issues:        NOT checked  #>  #> For details, inspect report$results$missing, $outliers, $duplicates, $numeric_like, $date_like   # With an optional date check df2 <- data.frame(   signup_date = c(     "2023-01-15", "2023-02-20", "not a date",     "2023-03-10", "2023-04-01"   ),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) report2 <- validate_df(df2, date_columns = c(signup_date = "%Y-%m-%d")) report2 #> < validation_report for 'df2' > #> 5 rows, 1 columns #> Checked: 2026-09-12 04:07:46  #>  #> Missing values:          0  column(s) affected #> Outliers:                0  column(s) affected #> Duplicates:              0  group(s) affected #> Numeric-like issues:     0  column(s) affected #> Date-like issues:        1  column(s) affected  #>  #> For details, inspect report$results$missing, $outliers, $duplicates, $numeric_like, $date_like
